_about: Manual faithfulness read of the 20 sampled alerts (reports/w03/alert_explanations.json, explain run b01f56c899314e2c94a1b12a3766eb2b). Each summary was read sentence by sentence against its evidence pack (attributions with values now and 72 h earlier, linked notes with classifier readings). A summary is faithful only if every stated cause, direction, number and quote is supported. 'auto_flag_valid' (LLM only): whether the automatic checker (v2) flagged the summary for a claim that is actually wrong. Read by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 2026-11-12; not yet independently reviewed by a person.
reader: Claude Opus 5.5 (session 2), not yet reviewed by Kuntong

A01.note: All drivers, values and 72 h values match. Quotes the newest of the four notes behind the 7-day note-count driver; true, but it puts a wifi note next to a vibration alert, which over-emphasises one note.

A02.note: Two drivers have no valid reading; stated as such. Faithful, but not actionable for an operator.

A03.note: Connectivity-note feature at 0 raises the risk (absence of notes); stated with its value and the 72 h value, and that no note is linked.

A05.note: Energy ratio 1.01 correctly qualified as essentially at the reference level.

A06.note: Quoted battery note is the one behind the strongest-fault-wording driver (battery is a fault class).

A09.note: Thermal-note feature at 0.000081 is a real driver of the model but carries no information an operator can use.

A10.note: Battery-note feature at 0.000006 is stated with its value; faithful to the model, misleading to read ('read as battery' with no battery note linked).

A12.note: Same near-zero thermal-note driver as A09.

A13.note: Quoted drivetrain note is the one behind the drivetrain-note driver.

A15.note: States 100 % risk: faithful to the model, but the calibration is overconfident (W03_Fusion_Results).

A01.note: Lists the drivetrain-note feature (a risk-LOWERING attribution) among the indicators of elevated risk and says it shows increased activity while it fell (0.293 to 0.179). Truncated mid-sentence; more than 3 sentences.

A02.note: Invents 'a trend showing increasing vibration' (no valid reading); says user-error notes have 'a strong negative impact' while they slightly raise the risk. Checker flag is a negation-scope false flag.

A03.note: Says notes indicate connectivity issues 'weighting 0.121': that is the value 72 h earlier; now 0 and no note is linked.

A04.note: 'Increased by 0.433 units' (0.400 to 0.433 is +0.034); invents 'wear on components', 'lack of proactive maintenance', 'better thermal management'. Checker flag (no service tickets) is a false flag: there are none.

A05.note: Invents 'above the threshold' for the motor-temperature excess; truncated. Checker flags are spurious ('ambient' inside a feature definition; negation).

A06.note: Says the fault note is 'from 72 hours ago' (it is within the last 72 h; 72 h ago the value was 0.001); calls a rising resistance 'consistently low'.

A07.note: Says energy use 'exceeds expectations' at 0.952 x expected and calls a 1.0009 x baseline value 'high'; says resistance is higher than expected while it fell. Checker flags are spurious.

A08.note: Presents the motor-temperature excess (a risk-lowering attribution) as a concern; invents '+16 %'; attaches the connectivity-note value 0.0565 to energy use.

A09.note: Attributes the temperature-corrected resistance values to the baseline-ratio feature and to '24 hours'; invents 'thermal issues'; presents the risk-lowering drivetrain-note feature as more relevant.

A10.note: Claims notes 'mentioning battery' (no battery note linked; feature value 0.000006) indicate 'a substantial concern'; invents 'ongoing operational challenges'.

A11.note: Calls 0.142 g 'slightly above the threshold of 0.143 g' (no such threshold; 0.143 is the 72 h value); attaches the no-fault-found value 0.404 to the thermal-note feature. Checker flag is a negation false flag.

A12.note: Claims notes 'indicate a thermal issue' (no thermal note linked; value 0.000066). Checker flag (drivetrain mentioned) is weak; the real error is not caught.

A13.note: Quotes a voltage-sag note (classified 'no fault found') as the drivetrain issue; '+25 %' for a 1.54 x baseline ratio; ambient 'risen from 38 to 34.9' (it fell).

A14.note: 'Increased the risk by 0.0624': 0.0624 is the feature value, not a risk change; calls a falling resistance 'high' and 'exacerbating'.

A15.note: Invents '+48 %', '+27 %' and an 'alert threshold of 15 %' for vibration (15 % is the risk threshold).

A16.note: Mixes the 72 h-earlier maximum (0.0698) with the current minimum (0.0529) into an invented 'significant drop'; adds advice ('the operator should closely monitor'), which the prompt forbids.

A17.note: 'Motor heating has risen by 9.76 %' (it is 0.976 x nominal, below nominal); invents 'overheating issues' and that the classifier reading says the issue was resolved.

A18.note: Says the strongest-fault note mentions a drivetrain issue (it is a battery note; the drivetrain-note feature lowers the risk).

A19.note: Invents 'two instances' of high vibration and says 0.239 g is higher than 0.250 g; says resistance 'dropped' from 0.0490 to 0.0500; presents the risk-lowering fault-wording feature as pushing the risk up.

A20.note: Invents 'inefficient operation' for 1.00 x baseline energy and 'mechanical wear'; garbles the 72 h comparison.
